correctness.rationale: An excursion has length T=L/max_i V_i and survival exactly F(L/a)^N, so the tail exponent is γ=Nα, including divergent mean at equality. Continuity makes the renewal law nonarithmetic. For any fixed H>0 the probability of an observation age at most H is bounded, for t>H, by the expected renewals in (t−H,t], which tends to zero by the infinite-mean Blackwell renewal theorem. To disintegrate, sum over candidate last renewals: the next speeds are fresh and last status at age a is exactly the product event V_i<L/a for all i. Thus the displaced fractions have independent truncated CDFs F(zL/a)/F(L/a); these tend to z^α as a→∞, including the endpoints. The conditional cloud consequently converges on bounded continuous tests, which yields the unconditional iid Beta(1,α) limit, and bounded position moments yield vanishing covariance. For 0<γ<1 the same conditional expectation argument against a bounded function of A_t/t factors the joint limit with the classical Dynkin–Lamperti Beta(1−γ,γ) age fraction. For γ=1 only divergence of the absolute age is needed. In the finite-mean exact power family, the equilibrium of the age-and-speeds process is normalized excursion occupation, with age density Pr(T>a)/ET; the renewal reward kernels for bounded continuous position tests are continuous and bounded by a multiple of the integrable decreasing survival, so the key renewal theorem gives the stated convergence. Z=min(A/L,1) then has density (γ−1)/γ on (0,1) and an atom of mass 1/γ at one. Conditional means are 1−αZ/(1+α) and conditional covariance is zero. Integrating Z,Z² gives (γ+1)/(2γ), (γ+2)/(3γ), and the stated positive covariance. This coefficient requires the exact power law; no infinite-mean augmented stationary probability is inferred. value.rationale: A shared first-arrival clock creates dependence even with conditionally independent particles. The theorem gives a sharp example where that source of dependence disappears entirely from unscaled positions while the clock still has a random macroscopic age, against a strictly positive equilibrium covariance in the natural exact-power family. The equality case and general low-speed robustness make the result more than a numerical or single-particle observation.
